title: Nearest-reference matching adapted for Corpus Pane
plainLanguage: Google’s pose-classification example shows a simple idea: normalize poses, compare landmark relationships, and find the closest stored examples. Corpus Pane can use that idea while keeping view and anatomical side explicit.
purpose: Strengthen reference retrieval without requiring a large new machine-learning system.

rules.statement: Normalize scale and translation before comparing pose features.
Compare multiple geometric relationships rather than raw pixel positions alone.
Do not silently mirror candidates; Corpus Pane’s anatomical side convention must be preserved.
Camera/view differences remain part of the comparison context because 2D joint angles change with perspective.

implementation.currentSupport: Corpus Pane 0.2.2.4 adapts nearest-reference matching with requested-region coverage, strict checked reference evidence, rough-query-only expansion, a combined pose-shape plus graded-view score, and explicit visibility-disagreement penalties. Neighboring views may outrank a worse same-view shape; clearly opposing views receive a strong penalty. Explicit hidden states remain useful knowledge but are not equivalent to visible geometry.
implementation.futureWork: Use the arm–shoulder–torso pilot to evaluate ranking quality against real poser-oriented decisions before adding more scoring dimensions.
